Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

tennis noun

also play tennis, tennis player, tennis match, backhand, doubles, singles, drive (tennis), fault (tennis), serve (tennis), set (tennis), out of bounds, tennis net

modern

Traupman 50, 392
M-O s.v. tennis (with a query, from Latham)
Andresian p. 19

tenisia, tenisiae f.

noun, first declension

To play tennis is tenisiā lūdere; a tennis ball pila tenisiae, the court campus tenisiae, the net rēte, the racket rēticulum (Traupman 50–51).

Other words

  • tenilūdium, tenilūdiī n. — tennis

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 50, 392

    Traupman’s other word; the player is tenilūsor (p. 51) or tenilūdius (p. 392).

  • pila rēticulāris — racket ball: tennis

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. tennis (with a query)

    A description from the racket, rēticulum, which Vives already gives for the racket of the old French game of tennis.

Examples

  • Quōmodo ergō percutiunt pilam? pugnō, ut follēs? — Nē sīc quidem, sed rēticulō.

    So how do they hit the ball? With the fist, like a football? — Not even that: with a racket.Vīv. Exerc. 22
